description: Group examinations by patient ID, with the examinations lacking an ID forming one group that counts toward the total and the average share; list up to 10 above-average groups by excess share.

b.request: Group examination records by patient ID, treating examinations with a NULL ID as one group; include every group in the total and in the average share. Return up to 10 groups whose share of all examinations exceeds the average group share, showing the ID, examination count, share of total, and excess over the average share, ordered by excess from largest to smallest, without rounding
b.sql: WITH group_counts AS (SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS examination_count FROM Examination GROUP BY ID), totals AS (SELECT SUM(examination_count) AS total_examinations, COUNT(*) AS group_count FROM group_counts) SELECT gc.ID, gc.examination_count, 1.0 * gc.examination_count / t.total_examinations AS share_of_total, 1.0 * gc.examination_count / t.total_examinations - 1.0 / t.group_count AS excess_over_average_share FROM group_counts gc CROSS JOIN totals t WHERE 1.0 * gc.examination_count / t.total_examinations > 1.0 / t.group_count ORDER BY excess_over_average_share DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: Group the examination records by patient `ID`, with examinations that have no patient ID forming one group of their own. For each group, count its examinations and work out that count as a fraction of the total over all groups. For the groups whose fraction is above the average fraction across groups, list the ID, the number of examinations, the fraction, and how much the fraction exceeds the average, sorted by that excess from largest to smallest, top 10 only, unrounded.
a.sql:
WITH group_counts AS (
    SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS examination_count
    FROM Examination
    GROUP BY ID
), fractions AS (
    SELECT ID,
           examination_count,
           1.0 * examination_count / SUM(examination_count) OVER () AS fraction
    FROM group_counts
), scored AS (
    SELECT ID,
           examination_count,
           fraction,
           fraction - AVG(fraction) OVER () AS excess
    FROM fractions
)
SELECT ID, examination_count, fraction, excess
FROM scored
WHERE excess > 0
ORDER BY excess DESC
LIMIT 10

c.request: Break the examination records down by patient ID. Which IDs have an above-average share of the examinations? Show the ID, its number of examinations, its share of the total, and how far above the average share it is, listing the top 10 by that margin from largest to smallest, unrounded. Group examinations by patient ID, with the examinations lacking an ID forming one group that counts toward the total and the average share; list up to 10 above-average groups by excess share.
c.sql:
WITH examination_counts AS (
    SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS examination_count
    FROM Examination
    GROUP BY ID
), shares AS (
    SELECT
        ID,
        examination_count,
        1.0 * examination_count / SUM(examination_count) OVER () AS share_of_total,
        1.0 / COUNT(*) OVER () AS average_share
    FROM examination_counts
)
SELECT
    ID,
    examination_count,
    share_of_total,
    share_of_total - average_share AS excess_share
FROM shares
WHERE share_of_total > average_share
ORDER BY excess_share DESC
LIMIT 10;

d.request: Group examinations by patient ID, treating examinations without a patient ID as a single group included in the total and average share. List up to 10 groups whose share of all examinations is above average, ranked by excess share from largest to smallest, with each group’s examination count, share of the total, and margin above the average share, unrounded.
d.sql:
WITH group_counts AS (
  SELECT ID, COUNT(*) AS examination_count
  FROM Examination
  GROUP BY ID
), totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(examination_count) AS total_examinations,
         COUNT(*) AS group_count
  FROM group_counts
), shares AS (
  SELECT gc.ID,
         gc.examination_count,
         CAST(gc.examination_count AS REAL) / t.total_examinations AS share_of_total,
         1.0 / t.group_count AS average_share
  FROM group_counts AS gc
  CROSS JOIN totals AS t
)
SELECT ID,
       examination_count,
       share_of_total,
       share_of_total - average_share AS margin_above_average
FROM shares
WHERE share_of_total > average_share
ORDER BY margin_above_average DESC
LIMIT 10;
